[RCLI.1.3] **Which options repeat, which are required, and which belong to an
implementation.** The grammar lets any option recur; this states what a
recurrence means.

`-L` and `-d` accumulate. Each occurrence adds one value, and the
values apply in the order given: search directories are searched in that order
and dialect files are registered in that order. Every other option that takes a
value takes one, and given more than once, the last occurrence wins.

`-o` is required by `compile`. `compile-project` writes
beside its sources ([RCLI.1.4]), and `dump-schemas` writes to standard output
unless `-o` names a file ([RCLI.1.5]).

A compiler may accept options and subcommands the grammar does not list. An
option it adds may only configure how it meets this surface — which toolchain
an emission step invokes, for instance — and must not change what an admitted
invocation produces. A subcommand it adds is outside this surface: no
obligation of this document binds it, and no other compiler owes it. Either
belongs to the implementation that adds it ([STYL.2.13.6]).
